dropped.item: "a schedule you can plan a life around": the explicit promise of a predictable, plannable schedule
"actually" in "nights that actually end": slight loss of emphasis on reliably finishing at night

changed.item: "running the kitchen when it counts" became "you'll run the kitchen when the chef's out". The original's vaguer scope (critical moments) is narrowed to specifically when the chef is absent.

"keep standards high without turning the kitchen into a pressure cooker" moved from a listed duty of the sous chef to a general restaurant preference ("We want standards high..."), which weakens the sous chef's ownership of it.
